public_rationale: The announcements establish that Anthropic published run-rate figures. They do not establish selective reporting of launch-inflated windows. Conversely, a trailing-window formula does not rule out selection through announcement timing. The available records do not settle the allegation.
limitations: Coinciding announcements and launches are not sufficient evidence of cherry-picking.
No evidence found of selection is not proof that selection did not occur.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic cherry-picks four-week API spend windows boosted by launches and annualizes them.

statement.excerpt: In simpler terms, Anthropic is cherry-picking four-week windows of API spend — ones that are pumped by big announcements and new model releases — and annualizing them.

from_speaker: pumped by big announcements and new model releases
our_interpretation: Cherry-picking means actual selective reporting of favorable measurement windows, rather than merely using a trailing four-week formula.
Selection could occur through choosing announcement dates even when the formula always uses the immediately preceding four weeks.
The relevant period is the February-to-early-April reporting sequence identified in the supplied context.
Overlap between a launch and a measurement window is insufficient by itself to establish selective reporting or a temporary uplift.
criteria.support_condition: Reporting-date choices, measurement windows, and revenue histories show that Anthropic selected launch-boosted periods to present unusually favorable annualized figures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comprehensive records establish a fixed, precommitted reporting schedule or another reporting practice incompatible with the alleged favorable-window selection.

evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Demand from Claude customers has accelerated in 2026'
evidence.explanation: This confirms a run-rate announcement during the claimed episode. It provides neither the underlying API windows nor evidence that the announcement date was chosen to capture a temporary launch spike.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated reporting policy or internal selection records, combined with API revenue across reported and alternative windows, establishing whether favorable launch periods were selectively presented.
